item.title: Early heat and drought stress can have lasting effects on corn growth
item.description: A brief period of heat and drought early in a corn plant's life can affect its growth and flowering months after the stress ends, according to new research from the Donald Danforth Plant Science Center and the University of Minnesota. The findings could help guide efforts to develop crops better equipped to withstand hot, dry growing conditions. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.description: Kanako Hosomura was working in a clothing store in Yokohama when an alert on her phone warned of an imminent magnitude 9.9 earthquake. “We all rushed outside,” Hosomura said, recalling how people poured out of nearby shops and offices to watch tall buildings and power lines for signs of shaking. item.title: 6933 reproducciones · 304 reacciones | Cómo China planea dejar de depender del mundo para alimentarse La seguridad alimentaria preocupa cada vez más a los líderes mundiales. Las hambrunas del “Gran Salto Adelante” y la “Revolución Cultural” marcaron al país y a su actual presidente, Xi Jipining. Ahora Pekín está impulsando la producción nacional de alimentos básicos, aumentando sus reservas y diversificando las importaciones. Brasil ya sustituyó a Estados Unidos como principal proveedor de soja, mientras China refuerza su presencia en América Latina. Además, la Iniciativa de la Franja y la Ruta funciona como una “Ruta de la Seda alimentaria”, con infraestructuras que facilitan el abastecimiento y reducen la dependencia de puntos de estrangulamiento. | DW Español

item.title: Rare hawks nest in California county after 30 years as abandoned farmland gets a new life
item.description: A California floodplain restoration project launched in 2023 has recorded its first confirmed nesting Swainson’s hawks in Shasta County in about 30 years. More than 32,000 native trees and plants were introduced across 150 acres of damaged land near the Sacramento River. Conservationists have also recorded rare indigo buntings breeding at the site, raising hopes for wildlife recovery. Fuente: The Times of India - World.

item.title: Climate change affects the quality of one of the world's most important staple foods
item.description: Depending on the cultivar, higher concentrations of carbon dioxide (CO₂) in the atmosphere can significantly alter the protein composition of wheat. This affects not only baking quality but potentially also the tolerability of wheat products. This is the conclusion of a new study led by the Leibniz Institute for Food Systems Biology at the Technical University of Munich. According to the study, the adaptation of crops to climate change should in the future focus not only on high yields but also on quality characteristics such as protein composition. The research is published in the journal… Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Warming could help make the Indian Ocean a stronger climate buffer
item.description: The world's oceans help slow climate change by absorbing carbon dioxide (CO₂) from the atmosphere, but how much they take up can vary throughout the year. New research, published in Geophysical Research Letters, suggests these seasonal patterns are changing across the Indian Ocean, potentially affecting how it helps to regulate Earth's climate. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.description: St. Johns County Utilities officials celebrated the completion of the State Road 207 Water Reclamation Facility. item.title: EPA quietly backtracks on claims US has phased out toxic Pfas compounds
item.description: Agency changes wording on website as Texas-based firm continues manufacture of plastic container barriers The Environmental Protection Agency has quietly backtracked on a claim that the US has phased out two of the most dangerous Pfas compounds – Pfoa and Pfos. item.description: Rapid coastal erosion threatens coastal homes and economies, and as Super El Niño rounds the corner, a town is reckoning with the reality of climate crisis San Clemente is one of southern California’s most picture-perfect beach towns – a capital of American surf culture since the 1950s. item.title: Retirement Fuels Bushland Restoration: Ken and Jill revive 970ha bush; older Australians follow
item.description: In their eighties, Ken and Jill Hooper have become dedicated stewards of bushland in Australia, showcasing an inspiring commitment to conservation post-retirement. Over the last twenty years, after acquiring properties in Victoria and New South Wales, they focus on enhancing biodiversity and curbing invasive species to safeguard native wildlife. Their work reflects a significant trend of older Australians contributing to community conservation, aiming to foster a legacy for future generations. Fuente: The Times of India - World.
